channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Trump touts his economy and U.S. actions in Iran in UNGA address
item.description: President Trump touted what he portrayed as international and domestic triumphs in a speech to the U.N. General Assembly.

item.title: Major news outlets banned by Trump will have their day in court
item.description: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are asking a federal judge to hold the president in check for what they say is a violation of their Constitutional rights simply because he doesn't like how they cover him.

item.title: Trump is on voters' minds in the midterms -- and they're not happy, poll shows
item.description: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds President Trump — and his unpopularity — is an outsize factor in why most voters say they want Democrats to win the midterms.

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy proposes energy truce with Russia during meeting with Trump
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met President Trump at the U.N. and proposed that Ukraine and Russia stop attacking each other's energy systems.

item.title: A look at the legacy and influence Nancy Pelosi will leave behind when she retires
item.description: Rep. Nancy Pelosi will retire following the 2026 midterm elections, ending her almost 40-year career in Congress, but leaving a lasting influence on U.S. politics.

item.title: China's Xi Jinping to meet with Trump at White House this week
item.description: As China's Xi Jinping meets with President Trump at the White House on Thursday. Talks will touch on Iran and how Beijing is circumventing U.S. sanctions.

item.title: In Utah, trails are being adjusted to allow adaptive bikes better access
item.description: New technology, including electric motors, means disabled people can get out on mountain trails. But those trails need to be modified to make them friendly for hand-cycles or three-wheeled ebikes.
